name: PARSeq (scene text recognition)
plain: PARSeq (Bautista and Atienza, ECCV 2022): reads one cropped word (Latin letters, digits, punctuation) with a Vision Transformer and a small decoder that refines its own guess; a base and a tiny version. Apache-2.0 code and weights.
summary: PARSeq (Bautista and Atienza, ECCV 2022): a ViT encoder over the word crop (32 x 128) and one two-stream Transformer decoder layer trained with permuted autoregressive sequence modelling; reads one cropped word or short line (94 characters: Latin letters, digits, ASCII punctuation; no space). Greedy autoregressive decoding plus one refinement pass, as upstream `read.py`. A recogniser only: the whole input is one line (one quad over the image); pair it with a detector (e.g. `ppocrv5-mobile` boxes) for full pages.

papers.title: Scene Text Recognition with Permuted Autoregressive Sequence Models

no_kernels_reason: the 26-step decoding loop is launch-bound, not kernel-bound, and portable already replays it as one CUDA graph (`cuda_graphs`, exports unchanged: `module()` is the plain network): 12.6 -> 3.6 ms (parseq) and 11.6 -> 2.1 ms (parseq-tiny) vs the original 19.6 / 18.0 ms fp16, same logits and memory; SDPA / cuBLAS are already the compute and no library in the manifests helps, so a kernels mode would only repeat the graph (measured 2026-11-15)
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: the text lines in reading order: a quad `[N, 4, 2]` per line, its text and a confidence `[N]` (text detector + recogniser; recognisers alone read the whole image as one line).
